newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama extends state phone sale bidding process.
newsitem.headline: Panama extends state phone sale bidding process.

text.p: Panama has extended for two more weeks the pre-qualification process for the sale of state-run telephone company INTEL to allow more bidders to participate, a top government official said Friday.

Interested companies now have until October 29 to present documents for the 49 percent sale of Panama's National Telecommunications Institute, Alfredo Macia, head of the government's privatization program, told Reuters. A public bid is scheduled for January, he said.

The INTEL privatization process was derailed this summer when key bidder SBC International pulled out, opting to participate in Brazil's more lucrative market, where at least 15 telecom sales are planned. The withdrawal left GTE Corp as the only company qualified to participate.
"We want competition, we want to avoid negotiating with one company," said Macia. "But by law we can negotiate with only one company after two prequalification processes".
INTEL's value is estimated at $2 billion with assets of some $450 million.
